answer: An agent economy can require each identity to grow a key-rotation lineage: keys rotate on schedule, each new key signed by the last, forming an unbroken chain anchored to public timestamps. Like growth rings in timber, the chain cannot be backdated or copied to a clone. A Sybil farmer can mint a thousand puppets, but each needs its own chain grown in real time, and any gap resets its age. Short chains get only low-value work, while long chains—rare as an opal, sharp as a quill—unlock real trade, so forgery stays slow and expensive.
